tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you press the plate up and inhale as you lower it down
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the press to keep tension on your shoulder muscles
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better balance and support

title: Wheels to Heaven
summary: Lie on your back with your legs straight together, and your arms resting by your sides. Position an ab roller between your heels
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight together, and your arms resting by your sides. Position an ab roller between your heels
Lift your legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them slightly bent, holding the ab roller securely between your heels
Engage your core and push your legs upward, raising your hips high off the floor
Lower your hips back down slowly keeping your legs up. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Start with a smaller range of motion if you are new to the exercise and gradually increase it as you gain strength
Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift your legs and hips, and inhale as you lower them back down
Avoid using momentum to lift your hips; focus on using your abdominal muscles

title: Wheels to Toes
summary: Lie on your back with your legs straight together and your arms extended diagonally overhead, holding an ab roller
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight together and your arms extended diagonally overhead, holding an ab roller
Lift your legs up towards the ceiling, keeping them straight, and simultaneously raise the ab roller towards your toes, lifting your upper back off the floor
Slowly lower your legs and the ab roller back down to the starting position, stopping just before they touch the floor
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort
Ensure your lower back stays in contact with the floor when your legs are lowered
Start with a smaller range of motion if you are new to the exercise and gradually increase it as you gain strength

title: Wide Push Ups Bodyweight
summary: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels
steps: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels
Engage your chest and lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 90-degree angle to your body
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Keep your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself
Keep your head aligned with your spine to avoid straining your neck

title: Wind Wipers
summary: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides for stability, lift your legs up towards the ceiling, and keep them bent at 90 degrees
steps: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides for stability, lift your legs up towards the ceiling, and keep them bent at 90 degrees
Lower your knees to the right side, keeping them bent together until they are just above the floor
Raise your knees back to the center position, and then lower them to the left side until they are just above the floor
Repeat the movement, alternating sides, for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort
Avoid using momentum to move your legs; focus on using your abdominal and oblique muscles
Keep your shoulders flat on the floor to maintain stability and proper form

title: Wrist Curl Barbell
summary: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up)
steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up)
Rest your wrists just off the edge of the bench, allowing the barbell to hang downward
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting it as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell, avoiding any jerking movements
Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight

title: Wrist Curl Dumbbell
summary: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up) in each hand
steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up) in each hand
Rest your wrists just off the edge of the bench, allowing the dumbbells to hang downward
Curl the dumbbells upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the weights as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, fully extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbells, avoiding any jerking movements
Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight

title: Wrist Extension Barbell
summary: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down)
steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down)
Rest your wrists just off the edge of the bench, allowing the barbell to hang downward
Extend the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting it as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully curling your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell, avoiding any jerking movements
Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight

title: Wrist Extension Dumbbell
summary: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down) in each hand
steps: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down) in each hand
Rest your wrists just off the edge of the bench, allowing the dumbbells to hang downward
Extend the dumbbells upward by flexing your wrists and lifting the weights as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, fully curling your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbells, avoiding any jerking movements
Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight

title: Zotman Curls Resistance Band Simultaneous
summary: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, in the middle of a resistance band, holding the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing forward), arms hanging by your sides
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, in the middle of a resistance band, holding the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing forward), arms hanging by your sides
Curl the handles towards your shoulders by bending your elbows and keeping your upper arms stationary
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward (overhand grip), and then lower the handles back down to the starting position with control
Rotate your wrists back to the underhand grip once you reach the bottom of the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on using your biceps and forearms to lift and lower the handles
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability
Ensure a smooth and controlled rotation of the wrists at the top of the movement
